title: Urgent patch: ephemeral credential fingerprint drift causing cross-tenant RBAC leakage in private clusters
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
During a private deployment control-plane sync window, ephemeral credentials minted for internal service mesh components were observed to have inconsistent fingerprint metadata after KMS envelope rotation. The inconsistency allows a stale auth cache entry to be accepted for a different tenant under rare timing conditions, leading to RBAC checks bypassing tenant isolation for short-lived requests. This surfaced as multiple customer escalations from two private clusters where operators observed unexpected resource access audit entries attributed to another tenant.

Observed impact:
- Cross-tenant access window up to ~90s under heavy control-plane churn (high severity for affected workloads).
- Audit logs for affected requests show tenant_id mismatch and an unexpected service-principal fingerprint in the audit entry.
- A small subset of private clusters (3 known clusters) with asynchronous KMS envelope rollovers and an older control-plane agent (v1.18.4) are vulnerable.
- Customers reported elevated security concerns and paused sensitive workloads pending fix.

Root cause hypothesis (current):
- Two independent issues combine: 1) KMS envelope metadata field used to compute the ephemeral credential fingerprint was changed in the new rotation protocol; 2) control-plane sync had a race where an old agent accepted a newly-rotated envelope but cached the wrong fingerprint-to-tenant mapping during a short window when the identity index was staled. The fingerprint drift means the same token signature validates but maps to a different tenant mapping key in the cache.

Priority and constraints:
- P0 security fix: patch must be validated, hot-deployed to private control planes, and accompanied by an audit backfill for affected windows.
- Changes touch KMS integration, control-plane agent validation logic, and the local RBAC cache population path. Coordinate with Security, Infra (KMS), and Customer Success for communication.

Acceptance criteria for the patch:
- Deterministic fingerprint computation restored and verified across envelope rotation variants.
- Control-plane rejects tokens where fingerprint-to-tenant mapping cannot be atomically validated at accept time (no silent fallback that accepts stale cache entries).
- New unit + integration tests cover rotation case, cache snapshot edgecases, and multi-tenant request flows.
- Hotfix rollout plan exercised in a canary private cluster with synthetic tenants before broader rollout.

Files / Artifacts / Links:
- GitHub PR (work in progress): https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/6123
- Runbook for mitigation and rollback: confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Priv+Credential+Fingerprint+Incident
- Alert dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/d/alerts/private-audit-drop
- Customer escalations tracker: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1PrivEscalations2026

Notes on scope reduction:
- This ticket focuses on the immediate validation + cache population fix and an audit backfill for the observed windows. A broader refactor of control-plane agent sync will be tracked in ENG-39240 (follow-up).
